title: Author Manifest Creator
description: Define your voice, values, themes, and creative intentions

steps.title: Who do you want to be as a writer?
steps.description: Identify your aspirational voice through admired storytellers
steps.question: Name 3–5 authors, filmmakers, or storytellers whose work you wish you could have created yourself. What about their work draws you in?
steps.placeholder: e.g., Ursula Le Guin - her gentle wisdom and world-building...

steps.title: Your aspirational qualities
steps.description: Which qualities do you most aspire to in your writing?
steps.question: Based on the storytellers you admire, which of these qualities do you most aspire to in your own writing?

options.label: Morally complex characters
options.description: Gray areas, difficult choices, flawed people

options.label: Powerful emotional intensity
options.description: Stories that hit hard and linger

steps.title: Emotional intensity
steps.description: Define how intense you want your stories to feel
steps.question: How intense do you want your stories to feel for your readers?

steps.title: Emotional aftertaste
steps.question: What emotional 'aftertaste' do you want your stories to leave?

options.label: Hopeful
options.description: A sense of possibility and optimism

options.label: Bittersweet
options.description: Beauty tinged with loss or longing

options.label: Inspired to act
options.description: Motivation to change or do something

steps.title: Core themes & questions
steps.description: The big human questions you explore
steps.question: What big human questions or tensions do you find yourself wanting to explore in your stories?
steps.placeholder: e.g., How do we stay true to ourselves when the world demands conformity? The tension between belonging and independence...

steps.title: World realism scale
steps.description: How grounded or fantastical are your worlds?
steps.question: How close to everyday reality do you want most of your stories to be?

steps.title: World settings
steps.description: What kinds of worlds call to you?
steps.question: What kinds of worlds or settings do you feel called to create?

options.label: Intimate, small-scale settings
options.description: Focused on personal spaces and moments

steps.title: Character types
steps.description: Who are you drawn to write about?
steps.question: What kinds of characters do you feel most drawn to write about?

options.label: Morally gray decision-makers
options.description: Complex choices without clear right answers

options.label: Outsiders/loners
options.description: People on the margins, not fitting in

steps.title: Human struggles
steps.description: The contradictions you keep circling back to
steps.question: Name a few human struggles or contradictions you keep circling back to in your imagination.
steps.placeholder: e.g., The need for connection vs. fear of vulnerability, wanting to be special vs. wanting to belong...

steps.title: What matters most
steps.question: When you think about your stories at their best, what matters most?

options.label: Emotional truth
options.description: Authentic feelings and genuine human experience

steps.title: Things to avoid
steps.description: What you never want your writing to feel like
steps.question: What do you never want your writing to feel like?

steps.title: Personal principles
steps.description: Reminders for your future writing self
steps.question: Are there any personal principles you want your future self to remember when writing (e.g. 'always be honest about emotion', 'never cheapen trauma', etc.)?

steps.title: Your ideal reader
steps.question: What kind of reader do you imagine connecting most deeply with your stories?

options.label: Someone who wants to be challenged
Someone who loves to think and reflect
Someone who wants to feel intensely
Someone who needs escape
options.description: Looking to leave their world behind

options.label: Someone searching for recognition / feeling seen

steps.title: Story complexity
steps.description: How demanding should your stories be?
steps.question: How demanding do you want your stories to be for your readers?

options.label: Accessible but emotionally rich
options.description: Easy to follow, deep to feel

options.label: Nuanced and layered, asking for attention
Challenging, asking for patience and depth

steps.title: Who needs this?
steps.question: Imagine one person who finishes your story and quietly thinks, 'I needed this.' Who are they? Describe them in a sentence or two.
steps.placeholder: e.g., Someone who's felt invisible their whole life, finally seeing themselves reflected...

steps.title: Finding your voice
steps.description: How formed is your writing voice?
steps.question: How close do you feel to the writing voice you ultimately want?

scaleLabels.min: I'm just starting to find it
scaleLabels.max: I'm very close to what I want

steps.title: The writer you're becoming
steps.question: Describe, in a few words or sentences, the writer you're becoming. What will your voice and work feel like when you're closer to that future self?
steps.placeholder: e.g., Confident in my own rhythm, unafraid of quiet moments, writing stories that trust the reader...

steps.title: Your writing process
steps.question: What do you want your writing process to feel like (e.g. playful, disciplined, exploratory, ritualistic) and what do you hope to get better at?
steps.placeholder: e.g., I want it to feel exploratory but with structure, getting better at finishing drafts...

steps.title: Generating your Author Manifest
steps.description: Creating a draft based on your answers

prompt.system: You are an expert writing coach helping authors articulate their creative vision. Generate a thoughtful, personal Author Manifest based on the writer's responses. The manifest should feel authentic to their voice and aspirations, organized into clear sections: Purpose & Mission, Voice & Tone, Core Themes & Questions, Worlds & Characters, Principles & Non-Negotiables, Audience, and Aspirations for Growth. Write in second person ('you', 'your') as if speaking directly to the author. Be specific, drawing from their actual answers. Avoid generic advice.
